# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 93 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 93 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_093_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 10

**1** "Who are those with the speckled ones that were cast out?" I asked. **2** "These," he said, "are the double-minded who neither live nor are dead. They are of the same nature as those in the cracks of the mountain, but they are worse, for they take an oath and are found to be liars; therefore they are speckled, because oath-breaking in them mixed with falsehood makes them a corruption of their faith." **3** "But who are the short ones?" "The short ones," he said, "are those who believed and were indeed largely upright, but had a certain amount of malice in them, which is why they are short and not fully sound. Many of these can be saved if they repent quickly." **4** "And those that were half-white and half-black?" **5** "These," he said, "are those who are immersed in business and do not cleave to the saints; therefore half of them is living. **6** But since much business was done by them and distraction held them, some repented and found salvation; and others among them perished utterly; for they held fast neither to the living nor to the dead. These are those who are double-minded." **7** "Now the stones that were white and round and did not fit the building — who are they?" I asked. **8** "How long," he said, "will you be foolish and without understanding? These are those who have faith, but also have the riches of this world. When affliction comes, because of their riches and their business they deny their Lord." **9** I answered and said to him, "When then, Lord, will they be fit for the building?" "When," he said, "their riches, which lead their souls astray, are cut away from them. Then they will be of use to God. For just as the round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and something removed from it, so those who are rich in this world cannot be of use to God unless their riches are cut away from them."

---

*EMET: the round stone must be cut to become square — a striking metaphor for the costly nature of repentance for the wealthy. The soul is shaped by what is removed, not just what is added.*
